scope: Linda logistics user intent; NO code implementation or new production connection

decisions.title: Transaction issuance trigger
decisions.statement: Linda starts when an eligible Odoo transaction reaches its machine-observable issuance/release condition. An Approved-like field is intended; its precise technical name is not asserted. Sales saying Ready is NOT the trigger.
decisions.evidence_quote: a field like approved or something mechanical that triggered Linda to send the po and so

decisions.title: Linda mechanically sends the orders
decisions.statement: Linda, not another human or upstream dispatcher, generates/resolves the applicable PO and SO from Odoo, renders Odoo PDFs, sends locked party-specific email templates and hands the work into Pending Logistics with true send status.
decisions.evidence_quote: it’s purely mechanical templates with Odoo generated documents

decisions.title: No routine human approval
decisions.statement: There is no extra human approval required for normal PO/SO emails, supplier/buyer/carrier requests or permitted logistical transitions. Distinct existing commercial rate/carrier commitment and financial controls are not silently revoked.
decisions.evidence_quote: No human approval. That was wrong

decisions.title: Existing Google Workspace mailbox
decisions.statement: Google Workspace is active by operator report and Gmail is the selected transport for logistics2@scrapmanagement.com. The account is intended for Linda; Odoo OAuth/alias/routing is not yet tested or configured in this pack.

decisions.title: Two-stage inbound understanding
decisions.statement: Standardized inbound emails use deterministic parsing. Free-form and complex inbound emails may use a bounded LLM as a semantic-to-typed-evidence extractor.
decisions.evidence_quote: A deterministic parser can handle the standardized replies. An LLM can help extract meaning from everything else.

decisions.title: Only deterministic validation governs actions
decisions.statement: Regardless of parser, candidate meaning is never a direct command. Odoo-controlled validators check source actor/request/version/company/business prerequisites, then allow the next routine action or clarification/exception.
decisions.evidence_quote: so Linda does the right next thing where it’ll be deterministic

decisions.title: Intent pack, not an implementation audit
decisions.statement: Product intent is compiled from accepted operator decisions and relevant donor sources. Current repository incompleteness is expected and becomes planned implementation work, not grounds to erase intent.
decisions.evidence_quote: We’re working on a user intent pack. Most of this isn’t in the current repo

decisions.title: Established timing and shipment rules retained
decisions.statement: Source-defined shipping cadence, shipper READY proof, appointments, three-PDF packet, double-blind routing and correct closeout remain in force as intent. Technical scheduling particulars not defined in sources remain unknown.

decisions.title: Technical execution strategy deferred
decisions.statement: Do not choose provider/model, transport integration internals, new database models, migrations, code changes, deployment, production sends or a technical implementation campaign during this user-intent revision.
decisions.evidence_quote: We’ll get to the technical stuff update the pack now
